newsitem.title: USA: US CFTC charges Florida brokerage firm with fraud.
newsitem.headline: US CFTC charges Florida brokerage firm with fraud.

text.p: U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission said Monday it filed a two-count administrative complaint charging Lexus Financial Group and the firm's co-owners with fraud in the sale of commodity options.

The firm and co-owners David Luger and Mark Singer committed fraud by making false, deceptive and misleading statements in radio infomercials and in telephone solicitations of customers, CFTC charged in its complaint.
Since Lexus opened in late 1992, over 88 percent of customer accounts lost money, CFTC said.
During that time, Lexus received $5.3 million in commissions, the CFTC said. The commissions represent 75 percent of customer losses, CFTC said.
The commission said it would hold a public hearing on the allegations.

Possible sanctions include cease and desist orders, customer restitution, trading prohibitions and revocation or suspension of respondents' registrations. Also, the commission said it could impose civil fines of up to $100,000 or triple the monetary gain to each respondent, whichever is greater, for each violation.
Kenneth Berg, an attorney for Lexus, denied the charges and said the firm will defend itself "vigorously."

"The performnace of Lexus customers is fairly typical of customers in the retail market generally," Berg said. In four years of operation, less than a dozen customers have filed complaints against Lexus, he said.
The firm's radio programs give a balanced presentation of the risks and rewards of commodity investing, Berg added.
